question: In the Basic Control Skills test, what is a 'pull-up'?
choice_a: Any time the vehicle stops without changing direction
choice_b: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_d: Backing up during a forward moving exercise
explanation: A pull-up is pulling forward on a backing exercise, such as Exercise 2 or Exercise 4, to clear an encroachment or to get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, Scoring

question: Are pull-ups penalized during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Any pull-up results in automatic failure
choice_b: Only the first pull-up is penalized
choice_c: The driver is not penalized for initial pull-ups, but an excessive number will count as errors
choice_d: Pull-ups are never scored at all
explanation: The driver will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: In which exercise is a 'back-up' -- backing up during a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position -- scored?
choice_a: Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking
choice_b: Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing
choice_c: Exercise 1, Forward Stop
choice_d: Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing
explanation: 'Back-ups' -- backing up on a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position -- are scored on Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What is scored as an 'encroachment' during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle, other than mirrors or unique parts above door mirror height
choice_b: Sounding the horn at the wrong time
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_d: Forgetting to set the parking brake
explanation: Crossing over or touching exercise boundary lines or cones with any portion of the vehicle -- other than the vehicle's mirrors, door, fender, or other unique parts at or above door mirror height -- is scored as an encroachment.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What counts as a 'look' during a Basic Control Skills backing exercise?
choice_a: Sounding the horn at the end of the exercise
choice_b: Checking the mirrors without stopping
choice_c: Safely stopping and exiting the vehicle to check its external position
choice_d: Asking the examiner for help
explanation: A driver may be permitted to safely stop and exit the vehicle to check the external position of the vehicle while backing; this is scored as a 'look,' and requires setting the parking brake and placing the vehicle in neutral first.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What happens if a driver opens the vehicle door while it is still moving (not in neutral or park) during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: It only counts as one look
choice_b: Nothing, as long as the door is closed again quickly
choice_c: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_d: It results in a warning only, never a failure
explanation: If a driver opens the door while the vehicle is in motion (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.1, Scoring

topic: The Four Basic Control Skills Exercises
question: What are the four exercises that make up the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, and Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: Forward Stop only, repeated four times
choice_c: Parallel Parking, Three-Point Turn, U-Turn, and Emergency Stop
choice_d: Uphill Start, Downhill Stop, Curve Negotiation, and Lane Change
explanation: The Basic Control Skills test includes Exercise 1 Forward Stop, Exercise 2 Straight-Line Backing, Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking, and Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.2, Exercises

question: In Exercise 1, Forward Stop, how many times may the driver stop the vehicle?
choice_a: Twice, with one free stop
choice_b: As many times as needed
choice_c: Only once
choice_d: Up to three times
explanation: In Exercise 1, the driver drives forward through the alley and stops with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end without going past it; the driver may stop only once.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.2.1, Exercise 1 Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, how far must the driver back the vehicle?
choice_a: Around a full circle back to the starting point
choice_b: Only halfway through the alley
choice_c: Backward and then forward again in a zigzag pattern
choice_d: Straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end
explanation: In Exercise 2, the driver backs straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, how many free pull-ups and free exits to check the vehicle are allowed?
choice_a: One free pull-up, and the driver may safely exit the vehicle only one time
choice_b: Two free pull-ups and two exits
choice_c: No free pull-ups or exits at all
choice_d: Unlimited free pull-ups and exits
explanation: The driver is allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around the vehicle during Exercise 2.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing

question: What must the driver do during Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Parallel park between two cones
choice_b: Drive forward and steer left through the opening into the opposite lane, keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line
choice_c: Back the vehicle through a narrow alley
choice_d: Make a complete U-turn within the exercise boundaries
explanation: In Exercise 3, the driver demonstrates the ability to maneuver around objects while moving forward, steering left through the opening into the opposite lane while keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking

question: During Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking, are free back-ups allowed, and may the driver exit the vehicle?
choice_a: Unlimited back-ups are allowed
choice_b: Two free back-ups are allowed, and the driver may exit once
choice_c: The driver must exit the vehicle to complete the exercise
choice_d: There are no free back-ups, and the driver is not permitted to exit the vehicle
explanation: In Exercise 3, there are NO free back-ups, and the driver is NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing, how close to the rear of the alley must the rear most part of the vehicle come?
choice_a: Within three feet
choice_b: It must touch the rear boundary exactly
choice_c: Within one foot
choice_d: Within ten feet
explanation: In Exercise 4, the driver offset backs into the alley, bringing the rear most part of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley, stopping in the three-foot box at the end.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed during Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: No free pull-ups are allowed
choice_b: Unlimited pull-ups and exits
choice_c: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_d: Two free pull-ups, and the driver may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times
explanation: The driver is allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around the vehicle during Exercise 4.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing

question: What is an example of an 'unsafe act' during the Basic Control Skills test that may result in automatic failure?
choice_a: Sounding the horn too loudly
choice_b: Asking the examiner a clarifying question
choice_c: Forgetting to set the parking brake, or opening the door while in motion
choice_d: Taking slightly longer than expected to complete an exercise
explanation: Committing an unsafe act -- such as forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion -- may result in automatic failure and termination of the test.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: What must a driver pass before proceeding to the Road Test?
choice_a: The Basic Control Skills test
choice_b: There is no prerequisite for the Road Test
choice_c: A written essay about driving safety
choice_d: A separate hazmat test regardless of cargo
explanation: The manual states the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before a driver can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13, On-road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: During the On-Road Driving test, which of the following must a driver do at all times?
choice_a: Avoid using turn signals unless requested
choice_b: Wear a safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_c: Drive as fast as safely possible to show confidence
choice_d: Keep one hand on the wheel at all times
explanation: During the test, the driver must drive safely and responsibly, wear a safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: If the test route does not include a certain traffic situation, what may the examiner ask the driver to do?
choice_a: Automatically fail that section
choice_b: Drive to another city to find the situation
choice_c: Simulate the situation by telling the examiner what the driver is or would be doing
choice_d: Skip that portion of the test entirely with no scoring
explanation: If the test route does not have certain traffic situations, the driver may be asked to simulate a traffic situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing if in that situation.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: What is considered 'unsafe coasting' while approaching a turn?
choice_a: The vehicle being out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_b: Slowing down smoothly while changing gears
choice_c: Using the turn signal too early
choice_d: Braking before reaching the turn
explanation: Unsafe coasting occurs when the vehicle is out of gear -- clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral -- for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: As a driver approaches an intersection, what should they do if it is necessary to come to a complete stop behind a stop sign or signal?
choice_a: Coast to a gradual stop to save brake wear
choice_b: Stop as close as possible to the vehicle ahead to save space
choice_c: Come to a complete stop with no coasting, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front
choice_d: Roll slowly forward until traffic clears
explanation: If necessary, the driver must come to a complete stop, with no coasting, behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front, and the vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the road test, where should the driver's vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Straddling two lanes for better visibility
choice_b: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), keeping up with traffic without exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_c: As far left as possible to avoid parked cars
choice_d: In the center turn lane at all times
explanation: During the urban business portion, the driver's vehicle should be centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.3, Urban Business

question: What must a driver do before changing lanes during the multiple lane portion of the road test?
choice_a: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and change smoothly when safe
choice_b: Change lanes without signaling if no other cars are visible
choice_c: Signal only after starting to move into the new lane
choice_d: Change lanes as quickly as possible to minimize time in the blind spot
explanation: During lane changes, the driver should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.4, Lane Changes

question: What must a driver do before entering an expressway or limited-access highway?
choice_a: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
choice_b: Come to a complete stop at the merge point
choice_c: Accelerate to maximum speed before checking mirrors
choice_d: Wait for a signal light before entering
explanation: Before entering the expressway, the driver should check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.5, Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: During the stop/start maneuver, once the vehicle is stopped, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Cancel the turn signal, activate four-way emergency flashers, and apply the parking brake
choice_b: Leave the vehicle in drive with foot on the brake
choice_c: Immediately exit the vehicle to inspect it
choice_d: Leave the turn signal on and keep the engine in gear
explanation: Once stopped for this maneuver, the vehicle should be parallel to the curb or shoulder and out of the traffic flow; the driver should cancel the turn signal, activate the four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and move the gear shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: Before entering a curve during the on-road test, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: Brake hard only once fully inside the curve
choice_c: Shift gears in the middle of the curve for better control
choice_d: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
explanation: Before entering a curve, the driver should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required while in the curve, and should keep the vehicle in the lane.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.7, Curve

question: If driving a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle, when should the driver activate the four-way flashers approaching a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Four-way flashers are not used at railroad crossings
choice_b: As the vehicle approaches the railroad crossing
choice_c: Only after crossing the tracks
choice_d: Only if a train is visible
explanation: As the vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, the driver of a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle should activate the four-way flashers.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: During the on-road test, within what distance from the nearest rail should a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: There is no specified distance
choice_b: Within 5 feet of the nearest rail
choice_c: At least 500 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The driver should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail, then look and listen in both directions for an approaching train.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: While any part of the vehicle is proceeding across railroad tracks, what must the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Checking mirrors after crossing
choice_b: Deactivating the four-way flashers after crossing
choice_c: Keeping hands on the steering wheel
choice_d: Stopping, changing gears, or changing lanes
explanation: The driver must not stop, change gears, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is proceeding across the tracks, and should keep hands on the steering wheel.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the on-road test, what might the examiner ask the driver to identify?
choice_a: The posted clearance or height
choice_b: The color of the overpass
choice_c: The name of the road below
choice_d: The manufacturer of the overpass
explanation: After driving under an overpass, the driver may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was; after a bridge, the driver may be asked the posted weight limit.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.9, Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: As a school bus driver approaches a student pickup during the road test, what lights and signals should be activated?
choice_a: The stop arm, before slowing down
choice_b: No lights are required until fully stopped
choice_c: Only the headlights
choice_d: Amber warning lights and the right turn signal
explanation: As the driver approaches the student pick up, they must decelerate and approach at a slow rate of speed while continuing to check traffic, and activate amber warning lights and the right turn signal.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.10, Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: During the student discharge exercise on the road test, how far from students at the stop must the school bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 50 feet
choice_b: At least 10 feet
choice_c: There is no set distance during this exercise
choice_d: Exactly 2 feet
explanation: As the driver stops for the student discharge, the bus must come to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop, then place the transmission in neutral/park, set the parking brake, and activate the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.10, Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: If a manual transmission is unsynchronized, what technique must the driver use when shifting?
choice_a: Rev the engine heavily before every shift
choice_b: Double-clutch when shifting
choice_c: Ride the clutch continuously between gears
choice_d: Shift without using the clutch at all
explanation: If equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, the driver must double-clutch when shifting, and should not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.11(a), Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Which of the following clutch habits is the driver scored against during the road test?
choice_a: Fully releasing the clutch after each shift
choice_b: Double-clutching on an unsynchronized transmission
choice_c: Using the clutch to start the vehicle from a stop
choice_d: Riding the clutch, coasting with the clutch depressed, or 'popping' the clutch
explanation: The driver should not ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or 'pop' the clutch.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.11(a), Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: Regarding gear usage, when should a driver avoid shifting gears?
choice_a: Before coming to a complete stop
choice_b: On straight, empty roads
choice_c: There is no restriction on where to shift
choice_d: In turns and intersections
explanation: The driver should not grind or clash gears, should select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine, and should not shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.12(b), Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What braking habits is a driver scored against during the road test?
choice_a: Braking early before a stop sign
choice_b: Coming to a complete stop at a stop line
choice_c: Applying steady, smooth brake pressure
choice_d: Riding or pumping the brake, and braking harshly instead of smoothly
explanation: The driver should not ride or pump the brake, and should not brake harshly, instead braking smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.13(c), Brake Usage

question: On a multiple lane road, in which lane should a driver finish a left turn?
choice_a: The lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: The right-most (curb) lane
choice_c: The far left lane, regardless of the center line
choice_d: Any lane on the roadway
explanation: Under lane usage rules, the driver should complete a turn in the proper lane on a multiple lane road, with a left turn finishing in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.14(d), Lane Usage

question: Under the steering scoring category, what must a driver do with both hands unless shifting?
choice_a: Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times
choice_b: Keep one hand on the wheel and one on the gear shift
choice_c: Steer only with the left hand
choice_d: Rest one hand on the window while driving
explanation: The driver should not over- or under-steer the vehicle, and should keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, returning both hands to the wheel once the shift is complete.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.15, Steering

question: When should a driver cancel a turn signal, according to the use-of-turn-signals scoring category?
choice_a: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_b: Only when the examiner asks
choice_c: Only once a new turn is required
choice_d: Turn signals should never be cancelled manually
explanation: The driver should use turn signals properly, activating them when required and at appropriate times, and canceling turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1.17, Use of Turn Signals

question: What can happen if a driver fails to follow the examiner's instructions during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: It may result in an automatic failure, and the test may be terminated
choice_b: The examiner will simply repeat the instructions with no consequence
choice_c: It has no effect on the outcome of the test
choice_d: It only results in a warning the first time
explanation: Failure to follow examiner instructions for completing an exercise as directed may result in an automatic failure, and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: During the On-Road Driving test, how are directions given to the driver?
choice_a: At the last possible second to test reaction time
choice_b: Only in writing before the test begins
choice_c: With plenty of time for the driver to do what the examiner has asked, and the driver will not be asked to drive unsafely
choice_d: The driver must guess the route without directions
explanation: Directions will be given with plenty of time for the driver to comply, and the driver will not be asked to drive in an unsafe manner.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested
